description: The conditional stage. A budget officer confirms the request has a PPMP allocation, stamps their signature and passes it to the Director — or rejects it, which is terminal. The stage exists only when a BUDGET_OFFICER account exists, and the Director can approve past it.

trpc_procedures.name: approveBudget
trpc_procedures.description: Stamps the officer's signature URL and the timestamp, then advances directorReviewStatus to UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW. masterStatus is deliberately untouched. The audit log records fromStatus and toStatus as the same masterStatus, because this stage is internal.

trpc_procedures.name: rejectBudget
trpc_procedures.description: Sets both directorReviewStatus and masterStatus to BUDGET_OFFICER_REJECTED — a rejection is visible to the requestor, unlike an approval at this stage. No signature is required to reject.

functional: The whole stage is conditional. If no BUDGET_OFFICER account exists, IDO's recommendation sets directorReviewStatus straight to UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW and this page is never reached.
Approving does NOT change masterStatus. The requestor's view says 'Director Review' from the moment IDO recommends until the director acts.
Approving requires a signature on the officer's profile; the URL is copied onto the request so the record keeps the signature that was used, not a pointer that a later profile edit would change.
Rejecting does not require a signature — a refusal is not a signed instrument.
Rejecting sets masterStatus too, because the requestor must see that the request stopped and why.
The Director may approve while this stage is still open, which ends the budget stage without an approval. This page must then open read-only and say the request has already moved on.
The IDO's decision — final title, reference, note, processor — is shown on the page.
budgetOfficerSignedAt is what the signature summary on the final approval page (spec 014) reads.
authorization: Server gate: roleProcedure('BUDGET_OFFICER') on both procedures, then assertPermission(APPROVE_BUDGET), then the stage check.
The stage check reads directorReviewStatus, not masterStatus — masterStatus is UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW for both the budget and the director sub-stages and cannot distinguish them.
An IDO officer or the Director calling approveBudget gets FORBIDDEN, even though both are staff and both can read the request.
The signature check is server-side. Disabling the button is a courtesy; the procedure is the gate.
ux: The approval is a confirmation dialog, not a bare button — it stamps a signature onto a document and cannot be undone.
A missing signature is explained on the page with a link to the profile, before the officer tries and fails.
The stage's read-only state names the reason: 'Already approved by you on 3 March' or 'The Campus Director has already approved this request'.
Reject is visually secondary and always asks for a reason first.
The IDO decision block sits above the actions, because it is the input to the decision being made.

edge_cases: The two-approver race is real and intended: budget-then-director, or director alone. The guards encode it — approveBudget requires exactly UNDER_BUDGET_OFFICER_REVIEW, while approveByDirector (spec 012) accepts either that or UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW. Changing either one breaks the pair.
The signature URL is COPIED onto the request. A later profile change must not alter an already-stamped approval, so never join to the user for a stamped signature.

Approving leaves masterStatus alone, so nothing in the requestor's view changes — the invalidation of myList and mySummary is still needed for the staff queue counts, but do not 'fix' the missing status change.
A budget officer account created after a request was routed straight to the director does not pull it back; the routing was decided at recommendation time.
The stage check must read directorReviewStatus. Reading masterStatus makes the budget and director stages indistinguishable and lets an officer act after the director has finished.

budgetOfficerSignedAt with no corresponding masterStatus change means this stage is invisible in the requestor's activity feed — that is deliberate, but it also means a rejection is the only budget event they ever see.
out_of_scope: The actual budget or PPMP figures — the system records a decision, not an allocation. There is no amount field and none is being added.
Reassigning a request to a different budget officer — there is no assignment model.
Any budget stage after the director acts — once past, it is gone.
